acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cached-binary path returns AlreadyPresent without invoking downloader or extractor.
Clean download path returns Downloaded, persists resolved paths via ISettingsService.UpdateAsync, and deletes the .partial directory.
Checksum mismatch throws InvalidDataException, deletes .partial, and does not touch the final target directory.
Missing RID throws PlatformNotSupportedException before any download is attempted.
Cancellation mid-download throws OperationCanceledException and leaves .partial intact while the final target dir remains untouched.
All new tests pass under dotnet test.

summary: Implemented FfmpegProvisioner.cs (13-step algorithm), FakeToolDownloader.cs, FakeArchiveExtractor.cs, and FfmpegProvisionerTests.cs. All 5 acceptance-criteria scenarios pass; full suite (47 tests) green with no regressions.

comments.note: FfmpegProvisioner.IsCacheHit calls VerifyAsync via GetAwaiter().GetResult() — a sync-over-async pattern that can deadlock in some synchronization contexts (e.g., ASP.NET classic or certain Avalonia pump threads). Consider making the cache-hit check async and threading it through EnsureAsync cleanly, or caching the checksum result on a background thread during startup.

The archive filename is derived from the manifest URL using Uri.LocalPath. URLs with query strings or encoded characters could yield an empty or confusing filename. A small sanitize-or-default helper would make this more robust.

ISettingsService interface uses SaveAsync but the plan/WP docs refer to UpdateAsync throughout. This naming inconsistency between documentation and code will cause confusion for future contributors — the interface or the docs should be aligned.

comments.note: IsCacheHit (FfmpegProvisioner.cs) validates only FfprobePath — it does not check whether FfmpegPath exists on disk. If FfprobePath is valid and its checksum matches, the provisioner reports AlreadyPresent and returns BuildToolPathsFromOptions, which falls back to options.FfmpegPath ?? string.Empty. A caller receiving an empty FfmpegPath would silently fail at runtime. Consider also checking File.Exists(options.FfmpegPath) before declaring a cache hit.

No test covers the Provisioning.Enabled = false short-circuit (Step 1 of the algorithm). This branch is exercised only at runtime. A single [Fact] confirming that EnsureAsync returns paths from options without calling downloader/extractor when Enabled=false would close the gap.

The inline comment in the extraction-cancellation catch block states 'Leave .partial intact; never the final target dir.' This is inaccurate: Directory.CreateDirectory(targetDir) executes unconditionally before ExtractAsync is called, so a cancellation during extraction leaves an empty targetDir on disk. The AC only tests mid-download cancellation so this does not constitute an AC failure, but the comment should be corrected and a test for mid-extraction cancellation should be added to document the real behaviour.

No test asserts that progress events are fired or that they arrive in the expected stage order (Verifying → Downloading → Verifying → Extracting). The progress path is exercised as a side effect of the happy-path test but no assertions are made against it.

summary: Reviewed 7 files across FfmpegProvisioner, HttpToolDownloader, ZipArchiveExtractor, TarXzArchiveExtractor, Sha256ChecksumVerifier, and both fakes. 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info findings. No blocking vulnerabilities. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/ZipArchiveExtractor.cs (line ~48) and TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs (line ~87). Neither extractor logs a warning when a Zip-Slip/Tar-Slip guard fires or when a symlink/hard-link entry is rejected. These are security-sensitive events that indicate a potentially malicious or corrupt archive. The gap is already self-documented as a TODO in TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs remarks. Remediation: inject ILogger<T> into both extractors and emit LogWarning for every rejected entry (path traversal, symlink, hard-link), including the entry name and the reason for rejection. This is consistent with logging patterns already used in FfmpegProvisioner.

A04 — Insecure Design / Incomplete cache-hit integrity verification. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/FfmpegProvisioner.cs, IsCacheHit method (~line 236). IsCacheHit verifies FfprobePath (file existence + SHA-256) but does not verify FfmpegPath. On a cache-hit, BuildToolPathsFromOptions returns both paths, but only ffprobe has been integrity-checked. A tampered or missing ffmpeg binary will be silently returned to the caller. Remediation: also check File.Exists(options.FfmpegPath) before returning true; optionally extend the SHA-256 check to the ffmpeg binary using the manifest's FfmpegRelativePath checksum, or add a second manifest field (e.g. Sha256Ffmpeg) to enable per-binary verification.

A04 — Insecure Design / No path-traversal guard on manifest relative paths. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/FfmpegProvisioner.cs, Step 9 (~line 195). FfprobeRelativePath and FfmpegRelativePath from ToolManifestEntry are combined with targetDir via Path.Combine without canonicalization or boundary checks. A value like '../../some/sensitive/path' would compose a path outside targetDir. These values come from trusted app configuration so the immediate risk is low, but a defense-in-depth guard (Path.GetFullPath comparison against targetDir) is recommended, consistent with the Zip-Slip/Tar-Slip protections already implemented in the extractors.

A04 — Insecure Design / DownloadVersion used verbatim in filesystem path. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/FfmpegProvisioner.cs, Step 4 (~line 105). The path Path.Combine(_appPaths.Root, 'tools', 'ffmpeg', provisioningOptions.DownloadVersion, rid) uses DownloadVersion without validation. A version string containing path separators (e.g. '../../../etc') would escape the expected directory. The value comes from trusted app config, making exploitation unlikely, but a simple guard (reject strings containing Path.DirectorySeparatorChar or Path.AltDirectorySeparatorChar) would eliminate the surface.

A02/A08 — No HTTPS enforcement on manifest download URL. File: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/FfmpegProvisioningOptions.cs (ToolManifestEntry.Url field). The URL accepted in the manifest is not validated to enforce the https:// scheme. An http:// URL would allow network-level eavesdropping of the download stream. The SHA-256 post-download verification still catches tampered content, so there is no exploitable integrity gap, but enforcing HTTPS is a defence-in-depth best practice. Remediation: validate that Url.StartsWith('https://', StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) before initiating the download, or apply a startup-time validation guard on FfmpegProvisioningOptions.

A04 — TOCTOU (Time-of-Check / Time-of-Use) on cache-hit path. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/FfmpegProvisioner.cs, IsCacheHit (~line 236). The SHA-256 hash is verified and then the stored path is returned; between these two operations a local attacker with filesystem write access could replace the verified binary. This is an inherent desktop-app design limitation (no OS-level locking) and is not remotely exploitable; noted for awareness.

summary: Code review FAIL — two blocking logic bugs found in IsCacheHit. Two non-behavioral comment corrections applied as Fix-Forwards directly. All other dimensions (structure, dependency injection, error handling, test organisation) are clean.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: corrected inaccurate comment in the extraction OperationCanceledException catch block. Previous text 'Leave .partial intact; never the final target dir.' implied the target directory is never created during extraction. In reality, Directory.CreateDirectory(targetDir) runs unconditionally before ExtractAsync, so a cancellation during extraction leaves an empty targetDir on disk. Updated to: 'Leave .partial intact. Note: targetDir was already created unconditionally above, so an empty targetDir directory will remain on disk after an extraction cancellation.'

Fix-Forward applied: corrected XML doc step ordering in FfmpegProvisioner class-level remarks. Steps 2 and 3 were listed in reverse order relative to actual code execution. The code must resolve the RID first (to look up the manifest entry) before it can perform the cache-hit check. Updated: moved 'Resolve RID; throw PlatformNotSupportedException when absent from manifest' to Step 2, and 'Return AlreadyPresent on cache-hit' to Step 3 — now matching the implementation.

BLOCKING — IsCacheHit uses archive SHA-256 to verify the extracted binary. ToolManifestEntry.Sha256 is documented as 'Expected SHA-256 checksum of the downloaded archive' (see ToolManifestEntry.cs line 16 doc comment). IsCacheHit uses this same value to verify the hash of FfprobePath — the *extracted binary*. In production, SHA-256(zip_archive) ≠ SHA-256(extracted_binary), so IsCacheHit will always return false, causing a fresh download on every application startup. The AC1 test masks this by passing sha256: FakeBinarySha256 (the binary's own SHA-256) as the manifest SHA — a test artifact that doesn't reflect production config. Resolution options: (a) Remove the SHA-256 re-hash from IsCacheHit and instead use file-existence plus ResolvedVersion == DownloadVersion as the cache-hit signal — appropriate for a desktop app where binaries are stored in a managed, version-stamped subdirectory. (b) Add dedicated per-binary SHA-256 fields to ToolManifestEntry (e.g. Sha256Ffprobe, Sha256Ffmpeg) so IsCacheHit can verify each binary independently. If option (a) is chosen, the AC1 test should also be updated to use ArchiveSha256 (not FakeBinarySha256) in the manifest to reflect real config.

BLOCKING — IsCacheHit does not check FfmpegPath existence. IsCacheHit verifies FfprobePath (file existence + SHA-256) but completely skips FfmpegPath. On a cache-hit, BuildToolPathsFromOptions returns options.FfmpegPath ?? string.Empty. If the ffmpeg binary is absent or FfmpegPath was never populated, the caller silently receives an empty FfmpegPath — a string that will cause a cryptic failure downstream when ffmpeg is invoked. Fix: add File.Exists(options.FfmpegPath) guard immediately after the FfprobePath guard: 'if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.FfmpegPath) || !File.Exists(options.FfmpegPath)) return false;'. This blocking issue exists independently of the SHA-256 design issue above and must be fixed in all resolution paths.

Sync-over-async in IsCacheHit: _checksumVerifier.VerifyAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult(). Sha256ChecksumVerifier uses ConfigureAwait(false) internally so deadlock is avoided with the current concrete implementation. However, the IChecksumVerifier interface makes no such guarantee, meaning a replacement implementation that lacks ConfigureAwait(false) would deadlock on any SynchronizationContext-bearing thread (e.g. Avalonia UI thread). Once the Developer addresses the two blocking issues, consider also making IsCacheHit an async method (Task<bool> IsCacheHitAsync) and awaiting it with ConfigureAwait(false) in EnsureAsync. CancellationToken should also be threaded through at that point. This was flagged by Developer and QA as well.

[documentation-forward] ToolManifestEntry.Sha256 doc comment ambiguity: the comment says 'SHA-256 checksum of the downloaded archive' but IsCacheHit uses it to verify the extracted binary. Once the Developer resolves the blocking SHA-256 design issue, the ToolManifestEntry.Sha256 doc comment and FfmpegProvisioner IsCacheHit doc comment must be updated to clearly document what value is expected (archive checksum vs. binary checksum) so future contributors understand the manifest schema contract.

AC1 test fixture mismatch: the cache-hit test uses sha256: FakeBinarySha256 as the manifest SHA (binary hash), while all other tests use ArchiveSha256 (archive hash). This is currently a test-only workaround for the production bug above. Once the blocking SHA-256 issue is resolved, ensure the AC1 test uses a manifest SHA value consistent with the resolved design — do not leave the inconsistency in place as it creates a maintainability gap.

Notable findings for Security Auditor: (1) IsCacheHit validates only FfprobePath — empty FfmpegPath can be returned silently on cache-hit.
